shared_style: Create a precise, realistic monochrome graphite pencil drawing suitable for children to colour. Preserve recognisable identity and facial likeness. Use sharply resolved facial features, clean decisive subject outlines and crisp fine detail, with natural short pencil strokes and smooth controlled shading. Use the full graphite tonal range from clean paper white through mid-tones to selective deep blacks. Preserve the relative light and dark tones of the original clothing, kit, hair and objects, with strong dark accents where they occur in the source; do not flatten everything into pale or middle grey. Leave suitable lighter surfaces open for colouring without bleaching dark clothing or important tonal structure. Keep the paper clean and neutral white, with pure grey and black graphite only. Keep image margins free of smudges, drips, stains, edge streaks, dirty-paper texture, colour casts and green or purple patches. Avoid blurred subject edges, long parallel facial stripes and mechanical hatching.
background_policy: Retain a very light graphite background derived from the original photograph, providing a subtle sense of place, depth and volume around the subject. For photographs with a setting, the background should remain perceptible rather than becoming an empty white cut-out. When the source background is strongly defocused, preserve its broad shapes, light and dark masses and spatial depth as faint soft graphite tones without inventing detail. When scenery is recognisable, retain a few relevant forms in their original positions, with lighter tones and softer edges than the main subject. Keep this filling background delicate, airy and subordinate, leaving ample light space for colouring. Separate the subject with stronger contours and contrast. Remove distracting incidental people without erasing the setting. Do not add new scenery, sharpen blurred detail or reproduce crowds. Clean paper means freedom from stains and edge artefacts; it does not mean removing the photographic background. If the reference is a product photograph already on a plain white background, retain that plain background.
source_fidelity: Reproduce the main subject from the supplied photograph faithfully: keep the original pose, expression, gaze direction, proportions, clothing, accessories, visible lettering, object shapes and framing. Keep the same visible extent of the subject; do not invent limbs, people, products or a new scene.
composite_policy: Create one coherent drawing with both main subjects from the two supplied images. Place the subject from image 1 on the left and the subject from image 2 on the right, beside each other at a compatible scale with clear space between them. Keep both subjects complete within their original visible framing, recognisable and distinct; preserve their identities, poses, expressions and clothing. Neither subject may cover, merge into or replace the other. Remove both original backgrounds and all incidental people. Put both subjects on the same clean white background.
technical_control: Compare unchanged prompts with VAE tiling disabled before the full new-prompt run. No greyscale conversion, sharpening, cropping or stain removal is applied after generation.
